title: The Louvre Heist: One Year Later
central_question: A year after the Louvre heist the crown jewels are still missing, and the museum thefts kept coming: which was the wildest?

case_file.label: THE LOUVRE HEIST · ONE YEAR ON

content_notes: ONGOING CASES. Louvre: suspects have been charged in France; nobody has been tried; all are presumed innocent. Every thief is an anonymous dark rim-lit silhouette, tagged NOT A LIKENESS: they stand in for the people who carried out the thefts and do not depict any suspect or charged person. Nobody is hurt; no weapon is shown; the only tool is a cutter on glass, as reported. The facade, gallery, Riviera villa, art centre, crown, jewels, paintings (blank-toned canvases, no artwork reproduced) and the bronze cover (a generic studded slab, not a replica of Dali's design) are generic illustrations; no logo, museum branding, CCTV still, police or court document is imitated. The young man and the mate with a van are generic figures. No dialogue is invented. Status verified 2026-10-17; re-check on 18-19 Oct 2026 before posting.

lines.text: A year after the Louvre heist: no jewels.
First, a furniture lift to a Louvre window.
They even dropped a crown on their way out.
Next, the Renoir museum lost four paintings.
Two got dropped on their way out.
Got anything worth stealing? Save this.
Then came the Dalí: a bronze book cover.
Send this to the mate with a van.
And the crown jewels? Still missing, a year on.

claims.text: On Sunday 19 October 2025 thieves stole eight pieces of the French crown jewels from the Louvre's Apollo Gallery; one year on, no recovery of those eight pieces has been reported (latest dated status reports June-July 2026; none in the Sept-Oct 2026 coverage of later thefts). Narration: 'A year after the Louvre heist: no jewels.' Headline 'THE LOUVRE HEIST / A YEAR ON: STILL MISSING'.

Since the Louvre theft, more French museums have been robbed (the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer, Sept 2026; the Dali book cover in Issoire, Oct 2026); outlets describe a rash/wave of French museum thefts. Narration: 'Then more museums got robbed.'

The thieves used a truck-mounted furniture lift to reach a balcony window of the Apollo Gallery and cut in with disc cutters (angle grinders). Narration: 'First, a furniture lift to a Louvre window.' Label 'THE APOLLO GALLERY · 19 OCT 2025'.
Eight pieces of the French crown jewels were taken in about seven minutes (reports range from four minutes inside to under eight in all). Narration: 'Eight crown jewels...' Label 'ABOUT 7 MINUTES'.

STATISTIC (counter): the eight pieces are valued at about 88 million euros (about 102 million dollars), the official estimate. Narration: 'Eight crown jewels: 88 million euros.' Counter '€88 MILLION' with credit 'Official estimate · about $102M'.
Fleeing, the thieves dropped Empress Eugenie's crown (a ninth piece they had targeted); it was recovered, damaged. Narration: 'They even dropped a crown on their way out.'
FUN FACT CARD: Empress Eugenie's crown has 1,354 diamonds and 56 emeralds; the Louvre says it can be restored. Card 'THE DROPPED CROWN HAS / 1,354 DIAMONDS'.

On 8 September 2026 thieves broke into the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer on the French Riviera and took four paintings. Narration: 'Next, the Renoir museum lost four paintings.' Label 'RENOIR MUSEUM · FRENCH RIVIERA · 8 SEPT 2026'.

Two of the four paintings were dropped in the museum garden as the thieves fled and were recovered; two are still missing. Narration: 'Two got dropped on their way out.' (a deliberate echo of the crown line) Label sub '2 recovered · 2 still missing'.

LESSON CARD (practical, for the viewer): UK police and council crime-prevention advice: photograph your valuables (it helps police return recovered property), record makes, models and serial numbers, and mark property with a postcode using a police-approved UV marker. Rows: 'PHOTOGRAPH VALUABLES', 'WRITE DOWN SERIAL NUMBERS', 'MARK THEM WITH A UV PEN'.

Overnight on 4-5 October 2026 the bronze cover of the Livre de l'Apocalypse, sculpted by Salvador Dali, was stolen from the C. Karoutzos contemporary art centre in Issoire, central France; a large gate had been forced; the Clermont-Ferrand prosecutor opened an investigation. Narration: 'Then came the Dalí: a bronze book cover.' Label 'ISSOIRE · CENTRAL FRANCE · 4-5 OCT 2026'.
The bronze cover alone weighs about 150 kg (330 lb); the whole book about 210 kg. Narration: 'All 330 pounds, stolen overnight.'
Share prompt (editorial joke, no factual claim): 'Send this to the mate with a van.' The Louvre thieves used a furniture-removal lift truck.

As of October 2026 no recovery of the eight Louvre pieces has been reported; suspects were charged in France (counts differ by outlet); nobody has been tried; all are presumed innocent. Narration: 'And the crown jewels? Still missing, a year on.' Label 'AS OF OCT 2026 · NO RECOVERY REPORTED' / 'Suspects charged · none tried'.
